question: Find the missing number: 4, 11, 30, 67, 128, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 219.

GIVEN

• Series: 4, 11, 30, 67, 128, ?

SOLUTION

• Test the cubes of natural numbers: 1³ + 3 = 4; 2³ + 3 = 8 + 3 = 11; 3³ + 3 = 27 + 3 = 30; 4³ + 3 = 64 + 3 = 67; 5³ + 3 = 125 + 3 = 128.

• So the pattern is n³ + 3. The next term is 6³ + 3 = 216 + 3 = 219.

• Check by differences: 7, 19, 37, 61, ? The second differences are 12, 18, 24, so the next is 30. Then the next difference is 61 + 30 = 91, and 128 + 91 = 219 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• When the terms rise slowly at first and then quickly, subtract a small constant (here 3) and check whether the results are cubes: 1, 8, 27, 64, 125, so the next is 216 and 216 + 3 = 219.

NOTE

• Option 2 (225) is wrong: it equals 216 + 9, but the added number is always 3 in this series.

• Option 3 (260) and Option 4 (285) are wrong: they do not fit n³ + 3 and do not match the second-difference pattern (+30 then 91).

• Cubes to remember: 1³ = 1, 2³ = 8, 3³ = 27, 4³ = 64, 5³ = 125, 6³ = 216, 7³ = 343.

question:
From the given set of alternative words, choose the one that cannot be formed using the letters of the given word. Each letter may be used only once; repetition is not allowed.

RECOMMENDATION
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. MEDICINE.

GIVEN

• Given word: RECOMMENDATION = R, E, C, O, M, M, E, N, D, A, T, I, O, N (14 letters). Letter count: R×1, E×2, C×1, O×2, M×2, N×2, D×1, A×1, T×1, I×1.

SOLUTION

• MEDIATE: M, E, D, I, A, T, E needs E twice (available twice) and every other letter once. It can be formed. ✓

• MEDICINE: M, E, D, I, C, I, N, E needs I twice and E twice, but RECOMMENDATION has only one I. It cannot be formed. ✗

• REMIND: R, E, M, I, N, D: every letter is available. It can be formed. ✓

• COMMEND: C, O, M, M, E, N, D needs M twice (available twice) and every other letter once. It can be formed. ✓

• So the word that cannot be formed is MEDICINE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• First list the letters that repeat in the given word (E, O, M, N here). Then look for an option that repeats a letter which is single in the given word. MEDICINE repeats I, which appears only once.

NOTE

• Option 1 (MEDIATE) can be formed: E appears twice in the given word.

• Option 3 (REMIND) can be formed: all six letters are available.

• Option 4 (COMMEND) can be formed: M appears twice in the given word.

• In "cannot be formed" questions, the answer is the word that needs a letter more times than it appears (or a missing letter).

question:
Read the two given statements carefully, followed by conclusions I and II. Determine which of the conclusions logically follow from the statements, ignoring any commonly known facts or real-world knowledge.

Statements:

All prisoners are men.

No man is educated.

Conclusions:

I. All prisoners are uneducated.

II. Some men are prisoners.
option_3: Both conclusion I and II follows
option_4: Either conclusion I or II follows
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Both conclusion I and II follows.

GIVEN

• Statement 1: All prisoners are men (A-type). Statement 2: No man is educated (E-type).

SOLUTION

• Venn diagram: draw the circle "prisoners" completely inside the circle "men". Draw the circle "educated" completely outside "men".

• Conclusion I (All prisoners are uneducated): prisoners lie inside "men", and "men" has no overlap with "educated". So no prisoner is educated, which means all prisoners are uneducated. Follows (A + E → E, so "No prisoners are educated", which is the same as I).

• Conclusion II (Some men are prisoners): the converse of "All prisoners are men" is "Some men are prisoners". Follows.

• Both conclusions follow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Rule: A + E → E. All P are M + No M is E → No P is E (which is the same as "All prisoners are uneducated"). Also A → I by conversion: All P are M → Some M are P.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only conclusion I follows) is wrong: Conclusion II also follows by conversion.

• Option 2 (Only conclusion II follows) is wrong: Conclusion I also follows from A + E.

• Option 4 (Either I or II follows) is wrong: the "either-or" case applies only when the two conclusions are complementary, and here both follow definitely.

• Remember: All A are B always gives Some B are A, and No A is B always gives No B is A.

question: Select the option which is exactly similar to: Flat 4B, 22-24 Brompton Rd, London SW3 1BW, UK; 01/05/'26
option_1: Flat 4B, 22-24 Brompton Rd, London SW3 1BW, UK; 01/05/26
option_2: Flat 4B, 22-24 Brompton Rd, London SW3 1BW, UK; 01/05/'26
option_3: Flat 4B, 22-24 Brompton Rd., London SW3 1BW, UK; 01/05/'26
option_4: Flat 5B, 22-24 Bromton Rd, London SW3 1BW, UK; 01/05/'26
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Flat 4B, 22-24 Brompton Rd, London SW3 1BW, UK; 01/05/'26.

GIVEN

• Given text: Flat 4B, 22-24 Brompton Rd, London SW3 1BW, UK; 01/05/'26

SOLUTION

• Compare each option part by part (flat, number range, road, city, code, country, date).

• Option 1: the date is 01/05/26, without the apostrophe before 26 ('26 in the given text). ✗

• Option 2: every letter, number and punctuation mark is the same as in the given text. ✓

• Option 3: "Rd." has a full stop after "Rd" (the given text has "Rd" without it). ✗

• Option 4: "Flat 5B" instead of "Flat 4B", and "Bromton" instead of "Brompton" (the letter p is missing). ✗

• So the exactly similar option is Option 2.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Compare in a fixed order: flat → number → spelling of road → full stops → code → country → date and apostrophe. A single difference rejects the option.

NOTE

• Option 1 differs by the missing apostrophe in '26.

• Option 3 differs by the extra full stop after "Rd".

• Option 4 differs in two places (5B for 4B, and Bromton for Brompton).

• In "exactly similar" questions, even a punctuation mark can make an option wrong.

question:
Identify which of the following entries are identical to the given address:

Ankit Sharma, 45, Rose Apartments, Sector 9, Gurugram – 122001

 

1. Ankit Sharma, 45, Rose Apartments, Sector 9, Gurugram – 122001

2. Ankit Sharma, 45, Rose Apartment, Sector 9, Gurugram – 122001

3. A. Sharma, 45, Rose Apartments, Sector-9, Gurgaon – 122001

4. Ankit Sharma, 45, Rose Apartments, Sector 9, Gurugram – 122001
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 1 and 4.

GIVEN

• Given address: Ankit Sharma, 45, Rose Apartments, Sector 9, Gurugram – 122001. Four entries are given and we have to find the identical ones.

SOLUTION

• Entry 1: name, number, building (Apartments), sector and city are the same, and the code 122001 is the same. ✓ Identical.

• Entry 2: "Rose Apartment" (singular) instead of "Rose Apartments". ✗

• Entry 3: "A. Sharma" instead of "Ankit Sharma", "Sector-9" with a hyphen and "Gurgaon" instead of "Gurugram". ✗

• Entry 4: the same as the given address in every part. ✓ Identical.

• So entries 1 and 4 are identical to the given address.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Eliminate the entries with an obvious difference first: entry 2 (Apartment) and entry 3 (A. Sharma, Sector-9, Gurgaon). The entries that remain, 1 and 4, are the identical ones.

NOTE

• Option 1 (2 and 3) is wrong: both entries differ from the given address.

• Option 2 (1 and 2) is wrong: entry 2 has "Apartment" instead of "Apartments".

• Option 4 (2 and 4) is wrong: entry 2 differs from the given address.

• Always compare name, number, building, sector, city and PIN code one by one.

question: Look at the matrix and choose the number from the options that should go in place of the question mark:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 63.

GIVEN

• Matrix: Row 1 = 11, 13, 143; Row 2 = 17, 5, 85; Row 3 = 3, 21, ?.

SOLUTION

• Row 1: 11 × 13 = 143. Row 2: 17 × 5 = 85.

• So in each row, the third number = (first number) × (second number).

• Row 3: 3 × 21 = 63.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• When the third number is large compared with the first two, test multiplication first. 11 × 13 = 143 and 17 × 5 = 85 confirm it at once.

NOTE

• Option 1 (25) is wrong: 3 + 21 = 24, 21 − 3 = 18; neither gives 25 and neither fits the rows.

• Option 3 (56) is wrong: it is not the product of 3 and 21.

• Option 4 (72) is wrong: it is not the product of 3 and 21 (3 × 24 = 72).

• In matrix questions, test the simple operations (product, sum, difference, squares) on the first two numbers of each row.

question: Complete the series: ADG, GJM, MPS, ____, YBE.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. SVY.

GIVEN

• Series: ADG, GJM, MPS, ____, YBE.

SOLUTION

• Inside each term, the letters move +3: A → D → G, G → J → M, M → P → S. So the third letter of each term is 3 more than the second.

• The first letters of the terms are A, G, M, ?, Y. They move +6 each time: A → G → M → S → Y.

• So the missing term starts with S, then S + 3 = V, and V + 3 = Y. The missing term is SVY.

• Check with the last term: Y + 3 = B (after Z comes A, B), B + 3 = E. So YBE ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Look only at the first letters: A, G, M, _, Y. The gap of 6 between them gives S for the blank. Only Options 2 and 4 start with S, and only SVY has the +3, +3 pattern inside.

NOTE

• Option 1 (SVW) is wrong: the last letter should be Y (V + 3), not W.

• Option 3 (RUW) is wrong: the first letter should be S, not R.

• Option 4 (SUY) is wrong: the second letter should be V (S + 3), not U.

• Letter positions: A = 1, G = 7, M = 13, S = 19, Y = 25 (the step is 6).

question:
If '+' means '×', '–' means '÷', '×' means '–' and '÷' means '+', then find the value of the given equation:

6 + 56 – 8 ÷ 45 × 8
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 79.

GIVEN

• Interchanged signs: + means ×, – means ÷, × means –, ÷ means +.

• Equation: 6 + 56 – 8 ÷ 45 × 8

SOLUTION

• Replace each sign by its real meaning: 6 × 56 ÷ 8 + 45 – 8.

• Apply BODMAS (division and multiplication from left to right first): 6 × 56 = 336; 336 ÷ 8 = 42.

• Then addition and subtraction: 42 + 45 = 87; 87 – 8 = 79.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Write the replaced signs under the original signs first, so that no sign is missed. Then use BODMAS: 6 × 56 ÷ 8 = 6 × 7 = 42, so the answer is 42 + 45 – 8 = 79.

NOTE

• Option 2 (68) is wrong: it comes from using the signs of the question without changing them (or changing only some of them).

• Option 3 (59) is wrong: it does not result from any correct step of the calculation.

• Option 4 (87) is wrong: it is the value before the last step (42 + 45 = 87); the last "– 8" was left out.

• In sign-change questions, replace all the signs first, then solve by BODMAS.

question: In the following question, a matrix of numbers is given. These numbers follow a certain pattern either row-wise or column-wise. Identify this pattern and choose the missing number accordingly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 6.

GIVEN

• Matrix: Row 1 = 84, 28, ?; Row 2 = 60, 20, 6; Row 3 = 72, 12, 12.

SOLUTION

• Row 2: 60 ÷ 20 = 3, and 3 × 2 = 6, which is the third number.

• Row 3: 72 ÷ 12 = 6, and 6 × 2 = 12, which is the third number. ✓

• So in each row, the third number = (first number ÷ second number) × 2.

• Row 1: 84 ÷ 28 = 3, and 3 × 2 = 6.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• When the first number is a multiple of the second, check the quotient first. 84 ÷ 28 = 3 and 60 ÷ 20 = 3 are the same, so the third number of Row 1 should match the third number of Row 2 (which is 6).

NOTE

• Option 1 (9) is wrong: it would mean the quotient is multiplied by 3 (3 × 3), which does not fit Rows 2 and 3.

• Option 3 (10) and Option 4 (14) are wrong: they do not come from (84 ÷ 28) × 2.

• Always check that the rule works in all the complete rows before using it on the incomplete row.

question: If EARTH is coded as FZSSI, then WORLD is coded as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. XNSKE.

GIVEN

• EARTH → FZSSI.

SOLUTION

• E → F (+1), A → Z (–1), R → S (+1), T → S (–1), H → I (+1).

• So the letters alternate between +1 and –1, starting with +1.

• WORLD: W + 1 = X, O – 1 = N, R + 1 = S, L – 1 = K, D + 1 = E.

• So WORLD is coded as XNSKE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Write the sign pattern below the word: + – + – +. Apply it to each letter in order.

NOTE

• Option 1 (XPSME) is wrong: it uses +1 for every letter (X, P, S, M, E), with no –1 steps.

• Option 3 (XNSMC) is wrong: the fourth and fifth letters should be K (L – 1) and E (D + 1).

• Option 4 (YNSND) is wrong: the first letter should be X (W + 1), not Y.

• Check: after Z comes A, and before A comes Z (the alphabet is cyclic).

question:
Choose the option that relates to the third term in the same way the second term relates to the first:

FAVOR : EBUPQ :: DANGER : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. CBMHDS.

GIVEN

• FAVOR : EBUPQ :: DANGER : ?

SOLUTION

• F → E (–1), A → B (+1), V → U (–1), O → P (+1), R → Q (–1). So the letters alternate –1, +1, –1, +1, –1.

• DANGER: D – 1 = C, A + 1 = B, N – 1 = M, G + 1 = H, E – 1 = D, R + 1 = S.

• So the answer is CBMHDS.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Write the sign pattern: – + – + – +. Apply it to each letter of DANGER in turn.

NOTE

• Option 2 (CZMFDS) is wrong: the second and fourth letters (Z and F) are shifted by –1, but the pattern gives +1 for them (B and H).

• Option 3 (EBOHFS) is wrong: the first, third and fifth letters are shifted by +1, but the pattern gives –1 for them.

• Option 4 (CZMHFS) is wrong: the second letter should be B (A + 1), not Z, and the fifth letter should be D (E – 1), not F.

• Cyclic letters: A – 1 = Z and Z + 1 = A.

question: If NOTE is coded as nOtE, then how is GAME coded?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. gAmE.

GIVEN

• NOTE → nOtE.

SOLUTION

• The 1st and 3rd letters (N and T) are written in small letters (n, t), and the 2nd and 4th letters (O and E) are written in capital letters (O, E).

• So the pattern is: small, capital, small, capital.

• Apply it to GAME: g (small), A (capital), m (small), E (capital). So GAME is coded as gAmE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Note down the case of each position in the example (s, C, s, C) and copy it for the new word.

NOTE

• Option 2 (GaMe) is wrong: it begins with a capital letter, which is the opposite of the pattern (capital, small, capital, small).

• Option 3 (GamE) is wrong: only the last letter is capital, so the 2nd letter is wrong (a should be A).

• Option 4 (gAMe) is wrong: the 3rd and 4th letters are in the wrong case (M should be m and e should be E).

• Case-coding questions test only the pattern of small and capital letters. The letters do not change.

question: In the following question, a matrix is given. A relationship exists among the elements in each row/column. Study the pattern and choose the alternative that will replace the "?".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 63.

GIVEN

• Matrix: Row 1 = 6, 9, 15; Row 2 = 4, 7, 11; Row 3 = 24, ?, 165.

SOLUTION

• Look at the columns. Column 3: 15 × 11 = 165. So the third row of a column = (first row) × (second row).

• Column 1: 6 × 4 = 24. ✓ (matches the 24 in Row 3)

• Column 2: 9 × 7 = 63.

• (Row-wise, 6 + 9 = 15 and 4 + 7 = 11 also hold in the first two rows, but the third row (24 + ? = 165) does not work, so the column rule is the one that applies.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• When 165 appears in the last cell, factorise it: 165 = 15 × 11, which are the numbers above it in the same column. Then 6 × 4 = 24 confirms the rule, and 9 × 7 = 63.

NOTE

• Option 1 (54) is wrong: it is 6 × 9, the product of the first row, not of column 2.

• Option 2 (72) is wrong: it does not equal 9 × 7.

• Option 4 (16) is wrong: it is 9 + 7, which is the row-wise rule and does not apply to the last column.

• Always test the rule on the cells that are complete (here 24 and 165) before using it to find the missing cell.

question:
In the following question, read the statement and select the valid  assumptions.

Statement:

The company has decided to allow employees to work from home permanently to improve productivity.

Assumptions:

I. Employees were less productive earlier while working from office.

II. Working from home will lead to better productivity in the long run.
option_3: Both I and II are implicit
option_4: Neither I nor II is implicit
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Only assumption II is implicit..

GIVEN

• Statement: The company has decided to allow employees to work from home permanently to improve productivity.

SOLUTION

• An assumption is something the speaker takes for granted when making the statement.

• Assumption I: The company wants to improve productivity, but this does not mean that employees were "less productive earlier". They may have been productive already, and the company only wants to improve further. So this is not implicit.

• Assumption II: The company has decided to allow permanent work from home because it believes that this will give better productivity. So it is implicit.

• Hence only assumption II is implicit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Ask: "Is the decision taken only if this is believed?" For II the answer is yes (the aim is productivity). For I the answer is no (improving does not require that the earlier level was low).

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only assumption I is implicit) is wrong: the statement does not say that employees were unproductive earlier.

• Option 3 (Both I and II are implicit) is wrong: assumption I is not implicit.

• Option 4 (Neither I nor II is implicit) is wrong: assumption II is the belief behind the decision.

• Remember: an assumption is a hidden belief behind the statement; do not confuse it with a conclusion or a fact.

question:
In the following question, one statement is given, followed by certain inferences. Consider the statement to be true even if it seems to contradict commonly known facts. Read the inferences carefully and decide which of them logically follow(s) from the given statement.

Statement:

Reducing screen time before bedtime improves sleep quality.

Inferences:

I. Excessive screen time before sleep may negatively affect sleep quality.

II. All sleep problems are caused due to screen usage.
option_3: Both inference I and II follow
option_4: Neither inference I nor inference II follows
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only inference I follows.

GIVEN

• Statement: Reducing screen time before bedtime improves sleep quality.

SOLUTION

• Inference I: if reducing screen time improves sleep quality, then too much screen time before sleep can harm it. So it is a valid inference. Follows.

• Inference II: the statement does not say that screen use is the only cause of sleep problems, and the word "All" is too strong. Does not follow.

• Hence only inference I follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Be careful with words like "all", "only", "always" and "never" in an inference. These are extreme and are usually wrong, while words like "may", "some" and "can" are usually safe.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Only inference II follows) is wrong: it makes an extreme claim that is not in the statement.

• Option 3 (Both inference I and II follow) is wrong: inference II does not follow.

• Option 4 (Neither inference I nor inference II follows) is wrong: inference I follows from the statement.

• An inference must be based only on the given statement and must not add any new fact.

question:
In a coded system:

· M ^ N → M < N

· M ~ N → M ≥ N

· M ! N → M = N

Given: P ^ Q ~ R ! S.

Which conclusion is valid?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. P < Q, R = S.

GIVEN

• Codes: M ^ N means M < N; M ~ N means M ≥ N; M ! N means M = N.

• Given expression: P ^ Q ~ R ! S.

SOLUTION

• Decode each pair: P ^ Q gives P < Q. Q ~ R gives Q ≥ R. R ! S gives R = S.

• So P < Q, Q ≥ R and R = S, which also gives Q ≥ S.

• Option 2 (P < Q, R = S): P < Q is true (from P ^ Q) and R = S is true (from R ! S). So both parts are valid. ✓

• The conclusion is P < Q, R = S.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Decode the symbols pair by pair and write the relations directly: P < Q, Q ≥ R, R = S. Then pick the option whose both parts match the given pairs exactly.

NOTE

• Option 1 (P < Q, R ≥ S) is wrong in the keyed answer: P < Q is true, and R ≥ S is also true as a weaker statement of R = S. (Flagged: because R = S, the relation R ≥ S is also valid, so Option 1 is not strictly false. The PDF key, Option 2, which states the exact relation R = S, is kept.)

• Option 3 (P ≥ Q, R = S) is wrong: P ^ Q gives P < Q, so "P ≥ Q" is false.

• Option 4 (None of these) is wrong: Option 2 is valid.

• In coded-inequality questions, decode each symbol first, then combine only the relations that share a common term.

question: Point E is 9m east of point C, which is 7m south of point A. Point F is 9m west of point D, which is 2m south of point B. Point A is 6m west of point B. What is the shortest distance between point F and point E?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 13m.

GIVEN

• E is 9 m east of C. C is 7 m south of A. F is 9 m west of D. D is 2 m south of B. A is 6 m west of B. Find the shortest distance between F and E.

SOLUTION

• Take A as the origin (0, 0) with east as +x and north as +y. Then B = (6, 0) because A is 6 m west of B.

• C is 7 m south of A, so C = (0, –7). E is 9 m east of C, so E = (9, –7).

• D is 2 m south of B, so D = (6, –2). F is 9 m west of D, so F = (6 – 9, –2) = (–3, –2).

• Horizontal gap between F and E: 9 – (–3) = 12 m. Vertical gap: –2 – (–7) = 5 m.

• Shortest distance FE = √(12² + 5²) = √(144 + 25) = √169 = 13 m.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Pythagorean triplet: 5, 12, 13. Once the horizontal gap (12) and vertical gap (5) are found, the answer is 13 at once.

NOTE

• Option 1 (10 m) is wrong: it does not come from the gaps of 12 m and 5 m.

• Option 2 (15 m) is wrong: it is too long; 12 + 5 = 17 would be the distance along the two axes, and the straight-line distance is 13.

• Option 4 (12 m) is wrong: it is only the horizontal gap and ignores the 5 m vertical gap.

• Triplets to remember: (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25).

question:
In the questions given below there are three statements followed by three conclusions I, II and III. You have to take the given three statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts.

 

Statements:

All Land is Field

All Field is Garden

No Field is Forest

 

Conclusion:

I. Some Garden is not Forest

II. All Land is Garden

III. No Land is Forest
option_2: Only conclusions II and III follow
option_3: Only conclusions I and II follow
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. All the conclusions follow.

GIVEN

• Statements: All Land is Field; All Field is Garden; No Field is Forest.

SOLUTION

• Venn diagram: draw "Land" inside "Field", and "Field" inside "Garden". Draw "Forest" completely outside "Field".

• Conclusion I (Some Garden is not Forest): the whole of "Field" lies inside "Garden" and has no overlap with "Forest". So at least that part of "Garden" is not Forest. Follows.

• Conclusion II (All Land is Garden): Land is inside Field and Field is inside Garden, so All Land is Garden (A + A → A). Follows.

• Conclusion III (No Land is Forest): Land is inside Field and Field has no overlap with Forest, so No Land is Forest. Follows.

• All three conclusions follow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Rules used: A + A → A (All Land is Garden); A + E → E (No Land is Forest); and the part of Garden that is Field is not Forest, which gives "Some Garden is not Forest" (E → O by implication).

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only conclusion III follows) is wrong: conclusions I and II also follow.

• Option 2 (Only conclusions II and III follow) is wrong: conclusion I also follows (the Field part of Garden is not Forest).

• Option 3 (Only conclusions I and II follow) is wrong: conclusion III also follows.

• Remember: a Venn diagram shows what is definitely true in every possible drawing. All three conclusions hold in every drawing here.

question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

 

Statements:

All Group are Team

Some Team are Club

No Club are Syndicate

 

Conclusions:

I. Some Club are not Group

II. Some Syndicate are Team

III. No Group are Syndicate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. None of the conclusions follow.

GIVEN

• Statements: All Group are Team (A); Some Team are Club (I); No Club are Syndicate (E).

SOLUTION

• Venn diagram: draw "Group" completely inside "Team". Draw "Club" so that it overlaps (cuts) "Team". Draw "Syndicate" completely outside "Club".

• Conclusion I (Some Club are not Group): the Club part that overlaps Team may lie completely inside Group, so it is not definite. Does not follow.

• Conclusion II (Some Syndicate are Team): Syndicate is related only to Club (as "No"), and it may lie wholly outside Team. So it is not definite. Does not follow.

• Conclusion III (No Group are Syndicate): Syndicate may overlap Group (the only restriction is that it cannot touch Club). So it is not definite. Does not follow.

• None of the conclusions follow.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• A + I gives no conclusion, and I + E → O* is possible only when the middle term is common; here the middle term links Team and Club in an I-statement, which gives no definite relation between Group and Club. So no conclusion about Group, Club or Syndicate is definite.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Only conclusion III follows) is wrong: Group may overlap Syndicate in some drawings.

• Option 3 (Only conclusion II follows) is wrong: Syndicate need not overlap Team.

• Option 4 (Only conclusion I follows) is wrong: all of the Club–Team overlap may lie inside Group.

• Test every conclusion in the most "difficult" Venn diagram. A conclusion that fails in even one valid drawing does not follow.

question:
Which of the following options should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order?

 

CFI, DHL, EJO, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. FLR.

GIVEN

• Series: CFI, DHL, EJO, ?

SOLUTION

• First letters: C, D, E, … move +1 each time, so the next is F.

• Second letters: F, H, J, … move +2 each time, so the next is L.

• Third letters: I, L, O, … move +3 each time, so the next is R.

• So the next term is FLR.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Treat each position as a separate series with its own step: (+1), (+2), (+3).

NOTE

• Option 2 (FIR) is wrong: the second letter should be L (J + 2), not I.

• Option 3 (FRL) is wrong: the second and third letters are interchanged (L and R).

• Option 4 (ELR) is wrong: the first letter should be F (E + 1), not E.

• Positions to remember: C = 3, D = 4, E = 5, F = 6; F = 6, H = 8, J = 10, L = 12; I = 9, L = 12, O = 15, R = 18.

question: Sunita’s mother’s brother’s son is Ritika. Then, how is Ritika related to Sunitha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Cousin.

GIVEN

• Sunita’s mother’s brother’s son is Ritika.

SOLUTION

• Sunita’s mother’s brother = Sunita’s maternal uncle (mama).

• The son of the maternal uncle is Sunita’s maternal cousin.

• So Ritika is Sunita's cousin.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Mother's brother → Uncle (Mama). Uncle's son or daughter → Cousin.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Aunt) is wrong: an aunt is a parent's sister (or an uncle's wife), not an uncle's child.

• Option 3 (Grandmother) is wrong: a grandmother is a parent's mother.

• Option 4 (Mother) is wrong: the mother is Sunita's own parent, and Ritika is the child of her uncle.

• (Flagged: the PDF spells the name "Sunita" in the first sentence and "Sunitha" in the question, and "Ritika" is usually a girl's name while the question says "son". These are copied as printed. The relation "cousin" does not depend on these.)

question:
Ravi is the brother of Arun. Sneha is the wife of Jai. Arun is the husband of Savitha. Durga is the daughter of Jai. Jai is the father of Ravi.

 

How is Durga related to Savitha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Sister-in-law.

GIVEN

• Ravi is the brother of Arun. Sneha is the wife of Jai. Arun is the husband of Savitha. Durga is the daughter of Jai. Jai is the father of Ravi.

SOLUTION

• Jai is the father of Ravi, and Ravi is the brother of Arun, so Jai is also the father of Arun.

• Durga is the daughter of Jai, so Durga is the sister of Arun (and of Ravi).

• Arun is the husband of Savitha, so Durga is the sister of Savitha's husband.

• The sister of one's husband is the sister-in-law.

• So Durga is Savitha's sister-in-law.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Husband's sister = Nanad (sister-in-law). Husband's brother = Devar/Jeth (brother-in-law).

NOTE

• Option 1 (Mother-in-law) is wrong: Savitha's mother-in-law would be Sneha (the wife of Jai), not Durga.

• Option 2 (Cousin) is wrong: Durga and Arun have the same father, so they are siblings, not cousins.

• Option 4 (Sibling) is wrong: Durga is Savitha's husband's sibling, so she is not Savitha's own sister.

• In-law relations come through marriage: husband's or wife's family members are "in-laws".

question:
In the following question, a statement is given followed by possible conclusions. Choose the conclusion that logically follows.

Statement:

Despite offering higher salaries, the company has faced significant challenges in retaining its top talent, leading to high turnover rates in recent years.

Conclusion 1: Offering higher salaries alone is not enough to retain employees.

Conclusion 2: The company is likely not offering competitive benefits or growth opportunities.
option_3: Both Conclusion 1 and Conclusion 2 are followed.
option_4: Neither Conclusion 1 nor Conclusion 2 is followed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only Conclusion 1 is followed..

GIVEN

• Statement: Even after offering higher salaries, the company has trouble retaining its top talent, and turnover has been high.

SOLUTION

• Conclusion 1: the company offered higher salaries and still lost its talent. So salary alone is not enough to retain employees. This is directly supported by the statement. Follows.

• Conclusion 2: the statement does not say anything about benefits or growth opportunities. The reasons for leaving may be different (work culture, management, personal reasons). This conclusion is a guess. Does not follow.

• Hence only Conclusion 1 follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• A conclusion must be directly supported by the words of the statement. Words like "likely" that bring in a new cause not mentioned in the statement signal a speculation.

NOTE

• Option 2 (Only Conclusion 2 is followed) is wrong: it brings in new factors (benefits, growth) that the statement does not mention.

• Option 3 (Both Conclusion 1 and Conclusion 2 are followed) is wrong: Conclusion 2 is only a guess.

• Option 4 (Neither Conclusion 1 nor Conclusion 2 is followed) is wrong: Conclusion 1 follows directly.

• In statement and conclusion questions, do not use outside knowledge about why employees leave jobs.

question: If 12 (20) 16 and 21 (35) 28, then what is the value of A in 48 (A) 64?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 80.

GIVEN

• 12 (20) 16; 21 (35) 28; 48 (A) 64.

SOLUTION

• 12 and 16 have the common factor 4: 12 = 4 × 3 and 16 = 4 × 4. The number in the brackets is 20 = 4 × 5. Here (3, 4, 5) is a Pythagorean triplet.

• 21 and 28 have the common factor 7: 21 = 7 × 3 and 28 = 7 × 4. The number in the brackets is 35 = 7 × 5. ✓

• 48 and 64 have the common factor 16: 48 = 16 × 3 and 64 = 16 × 4. So A = 16 × 5 = 80.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• The middle number is the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose sides are the outer numbers: √(12² + 16²) = √400 = 20; √(21² + 28²) = √1225 = 35; √(48² + 64²) = √6400 = 80.

NOTE

• Option 1 (72) is wrong: it is not the square root of 48² + 64².

• Option 3 (96) is wrong: it is 48 × 2 and does not fit the earlier examples.

• Option 4 (60) is wrong: it is not the hypotenuse for 48 and 64 (it would belong to the sides 36 and 48).

• Triplet (3, 4, 5) multiplied by 4, 7 and 16 gives (12, 16, 20), (21, 28, 35) and (48, 64, 80).

question:
In the following question, three statements are given, followed by four conclusions, I, II, III and IV. Consider the statements to be true even if they appear to contradict commonly known facts. Based on the given statements, determine which conclusion(s) logically follow. Choose your answer from the options provided.

Statements:

I. All inductors are condensers.

II. Some resistors are inductors.

III. All atomic numbers are resistors.

Conclusions:

I. All atomic numbers are condensers.

II. Some atomic numbers are condensers.

III. Some condensers are resistors.

IV. All resistors are condensers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Only Conclusion III follows.

GIVEN

• Statements: All inductors are condensers (A); Some resistors are inductors (I); All atomic numbers are resistors (A).

SOLUTION

• Venn diagram: draw "inductors" completely inside "condensers". Draw "resistors" so that it overlaps (cuts) "inductors". Draw "atomic numbers" completely inside "resistors".

• Statements II and I combine as: Some resistors are inductors + All inductors are condensers → Some resistors are condensers (I + A → I). Its converse is Some condensers are resistors.

• Conclusion I (All atomic numbers are condensers): atomic numbers are inside resistors, but they may lie in the part of resistors that is outside inductors. Not definite. Does not follow.

• Conclusion II (Some atomic numbers are condensers): atomic numbers may lie completely outside the overlap with condensers. Not definite. Does not follow.

• Conclusion III (Some condensers are resistors): follows from I + A → I and its conversion. Follows.

• Conclusion IV (All resistors are condensers): only some resistors are inductors, so the others may be outside condensers. Does not follow.

• Only Conclusion III follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Rules: I + A → I (Some resistors are condensers), then convert the I-statement (Some condensers are resistors). A conclusion that uses "All" for the resistors, or links atomic numbers with condensers, is not definite.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only Conclusion I follows) is wrong: atomic numbers may lie in the part of resistors that is outside inductors.

• Option 2 (Only Conclusion II follows) is wrong: atomic numbers need not overlap with condensers.

• Option 4 (Only Conclusion IV follows) is wrong: only "some" resistors are inductors, so "All resistors are condensers" is not definite.

• Remember: a particular (I) statement can never give a universal (A) conclusion.

question: Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (QUAD) was originally proposed in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2007.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (QUAD) was originally proposed in 2007 by the then Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe.

 

• The four member countries are India, the United States, Japan and Australia.

 

• The idea grew out of the joint tsunami relief work of these four countries after the Indian Ocean tsunami of December 2004.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Quad lapsed in 2008 when Australia withdrew. It was revived in November 2017 on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit in Manila.

 

• The first virtual Quad Leaders' Summit was held on 12 March 2021, and the first in-person Leaders' Summit was held in Washington in September 2021.

 

• The Quad is an informal strategic grouping that focuses on a free, open and inclusive Indo-Pacific. It is not a military alliance.

 

• Malabar is a naval exercise held among India, the US, Japan and Australia.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (2005) is wrong: the Quad was proposed two years later, in 2007. The tsunami cooperation of 2004–05 only formed the background.

 

• Option 3 (2010) is wrong: the Quad was inactive at that time (it had lapsed in 2008).

 

• Option 4 (2015) is wrong: Japan became a permanent partner in the Malabar exercise in 2015, but the Quad itself was proposed in 2007 and revived in 2017.

question: The Human Development Index (HDI) is released by which organization?
solution_text:
The correct answer is United Nations Development Programme.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Human Development Index (HDI) is released by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in its annual Human Development Report.

 

• The HDI was developed by the Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq with the Indian economist Amartya Sen. It was first published in 1990.

 

• It measures a country's progress using three dimensions: a long and healthy life (life expectancy at birth), knowledge (mean and expected years of schooling) and a decent standard of living (GNI per capita).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The HDI value lies between 0 and 1. A value closer to 1 shows higher human development. The UNDP groups countries as very high, high, medium and low human development.

 

• The UNDP headquarters is in New York.

 

• Related index: the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is released by the UNDP along with the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (International Monetary Fund) is wrong: the IMF releases the World Economic Outlook and does not publish the HDI.

 

• Option 3 (World Health Organization) is wrong: the WHO releases health reports (for example, the World Health Statistics).

 

• Option 4 (World Economic Forum) is wrong: the WEF releases the Global Gender Gap Report and the Global Risks Report, not the HDI.

question: Which nation remained at the very bottom of the happiness rankings in the World Happiness Report 2026, making it the unhappiest country globally?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Afghanistan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the World Happiness Report 2026, Afghanistan was again ranked at the bottom, which makes it the least happy country in the world. (Zimbabwe and Lebanon were also among the lowest-ranked countries in the report.)

 

• The World Happiness Report is released every year on 20 March, the International Day of Happiness. It is produced by the Wellbeing Research Centre at the University of Oxford with Gallup and the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN).

 

• The rankings are based on the average of how people rate their own lives over three years (the Cantril ladder), along with factors such as social support, income, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity and perceptions of corruption.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The International Day of Happiness is observed on 20 March every year. It was declared by the UN General Assembly in 2012.

 

• Bhutan is known for the concept of Gross National Happiness (GNH), introduced by King Jigme Singye Wangchuck.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Yemen) is wrong: Yemen has a low rank, but it is not at the very bottom of the 2026 list.

 

• Option 3 (Sierra Leone) is wrong: Sierra Leone is among the low-ranked countries, but it is not the last.

 

• Option 4 (Lebanon) is wrong: Lebanon is among the three lowest-ranked countries, but Afghanistan is below it.

question: Which mission preceded the LVM3-M5 flight of the LVM3 rocket?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandrayaan-3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The LVM3-M5 flight (launched on 2 November 2025 from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota) carried the communication satellite CMS-03 (GSAT-7R), the heaviest satellite launched from India so far (about 4,400 kg).

 

• The LVM3 flight before it was LVM3-M4, which launched Chandrayaan-3 on 14 July 2023. So Chandrayaan-3 preceded LVM3-M5.

 

• LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3, earlier GSLV Mk III) is a three-stage heavy-lift launcher of ISRO. It is nicknamed "Bahubali".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chandrayaan-3 made a soft landing near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023. India became the fourth country to land on the Moon and the first to land near the south pole.

 

• LVM3 also launched OneWeb satellites in 2022 and 2023 (LVM3-M2 and LVM3-M3).

 

• The human-rated version of LVM3 (HRLV) is planned for the Gaganyaan crewed mission.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Gaganyaan-D1) is wrong: the Gaganyaan test-vehicle missions are separate and use a test vehicle, not an LVM3 flight before M5.

 

• Option 3 (Aditya-L1) is wrong: Aditya-L1 was launched on a PSLV rocket (PSLV-C57) in September 2023.

 

• Option 4 (SSLV-D2) is wrong: SSLV-D2 was a flight of the Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (February 2023), not of LVM3.

question:
Fill in the blank:

As per the 2011 Census, the average density of population in India is ___ persons per sq km.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 382 persons per sq km.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the 2011 Census, the average density of population in India is 382 persons per sq km (it was 325 in 2001).

 

• Population density = total population ÷ total area. India's population in 2011 was about 121 crore (1,210.8 million) and the area is about 3.28 million sq km.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Among the states, Bihar has the highest density (about 1,100 persons per sq km). Arunachal Pradesh has the lowest density (17 persons per sq km).

 

• Among the Union Territories, the National Capital Territory of Delhi has the highest density (about 11,300 persons per sq km).

 

• The density of population in 1951 was 117 persons per sq km. It has risen with every census.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (117 persons per sq km) is wrong: this was the density in 1951 and not in 2011.

 

• Option 2 (200 persons per sq km) is wrong: it does not match the density of any recent census.

 

• Option 4 (828 persons per sq km) is wrong: it is far above the national average and does not match the 2011 figure.

question: Which term refers to the excess of government expenditure over its receipts excluding borrowings?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fiscal deficit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure of the government – Total receipts excluding borrowings (that is, revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts). It shows the total amount that the government has to borrow in a year.

 

• The fiscal deficit is the key measure of the government's borrowing need. It is usually shown as a percentage of GDP.

 

• The FRBM Act, 2003 (Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act) sets targets to reduce the fiscal deficit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure – Revenue receipts.

 

• Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit – Interest payments. It shows the borrowing needed apart from interest on past debt.

 

• Effective revenue deficit = Revenue deficit – Grants for creation of capital assets.

 

• If the fiscal deficit is financed by borrowing, it adds to the public debt.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Revenue deficit) is wrong: it compares only revenue expenditure with revenue receipts and does not include capital items.

 

• Option 3 (Primary deficit) is wrong: it is the fiscal deficit minus interest payments, so it is smaller than the fiscal deficit.

 

• Option 4 (Budget deficit) is wrong: it is an older concept (total expenditure minus total receipts), which is no longer used in the Union Budget of India.

question:
Fill in the blank:

Payments made by the government without any goods or services in return are called __ payments.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Transfer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Payments made by the government for which it receives no goods or services in return are called transfer payments. Examples are pensions, scholarships, unemployment allowances and subsidies.

 

• These payments only transfer income from one group (taxpayers) to another (beneficiaries). They are not included in the national income (GDP) because no output is produced against them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• In contrast, payments made for goods and services (for example, salaries of government employees, purchase of defence equipment) are not transfer payments.

 

• Transfer payments are a part of the government's revenue expenditure in the Union Budget.

 

• In the national income, transfer payments are not counted in the government's final consumption expenditure.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (Revenue) is wrong: "revenue payments" or revenue expenditure is a wider term (it includes salaries, interest and subsidies) and it does not by itself mean "no return".

 

• Option 3 (Capital) is wrong: capital payments (such as building roads) create assets.

 

• Option 4 (Subsidy) is wrong: a subsidy is one kind of transfer payment, but the general term for such payments is "transfer payments".

question: What was the target growth rate versus the actual growth rate for the Sixth Five-Year Plan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Target: 5.2%, Actual: 5.7%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–85) had a target growth rate of 5.2% and achieved an actual growth rate of 5.7%.

 

• The Plan's main aims were poverty removal and self-reliance. The Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP) and the National Rural Employment Programme (NREP) were launched in this Plan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fifth Plan (1974–79): target 4.4%, actual 4.8%.

 

• Seventh Plan (1985–90): target 5.0%, actual about 6.0%.

 

• Eighth Plan (1992–97): target 5.6%, actual about 6.8%.

 

• The Five-Year Plans were replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015. The Twelfth Plan (2012–17) was the last.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (4.4%, 4.8%) is wrong: these are the figures of the Fifth Plan.

 

• Option 3 (5.0%, 6.0%) is wrong: these are the figures of the Seventh Plan.

 

• Option 4 (5.6%, 6.8%) is wrong: these are the figures of the Eighth Plan.

question: At present, how many National Waterways have been declared in India under the National Waterways Act, 2016?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 111.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Waterways Act, 2016 declared 111 inland waterways as National Waterways (NWs) in India. Before this Act there were only 5 National Waterways.

 

• The Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), established in 1986, develops and regulates the National Waterways. Its headquarters is at Noida.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NW-1: Ganga–Bhagirathi–Hooghly (Haldia to Prayagraj). NW-2: Brahmaputra (Dhubri to Sadiya). NW-3: West Coast Canal (Kottapuram to Kollam). NW-4: Kakinada–Puducherry stretch of canals. NW-5: East Coast Canal with Brahmani river and Mahanadi delta rivers.

 

• NW-1 is the longest of the original five (about 1,620 km).

 

• The National Waterways Act, 2016 repealed the earlier Acts that had declared the five waterways.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (121) is wrong: the number declared under the 2016 Act is 111.

 

• Option 3 (212) is wrong: it is not the number of National Waterways declared.

 

• Option 4 (132) is wrong: it is not the number of National Waterways declared.

question: Which of the following punishments is newly introduced in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Community service.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Community service is newly introduced as a form of punishment in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. It is given for petty offences, for example, attempt to commit suicide (Section 226) and petty theft by a first-time offender.

 

• The BNS replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and came into force on 1 July 2024.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three new criminal laws that came into force on 1 July 2024 are the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (replacing the IPC), the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (replacing the CrPC) and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (replacing the Indian Evidence Act, 1872).

 

• The BNS also added new offences such as organised crime, terrorism, mob lynching and snatching.

 

• Section 4 of the BNS lists the punishments: death, imprisonment for life, imprisonment (rigorous or simple), forfeiture of property, fine and community service.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Monetary fine penalty) is wrong: a fine was already a punishment under the IPC.

 

• Option 2 (Forfeiture of property) is wrong: it was already listed in the IPC (Section 53).

 

• Option 4 (Rigorous imprisonment) is wrong: it was already a punishment under the IPC.

question: Which earthquake waves travel fastest through the Earth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Primary waves arriving first always.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Primary waves (P-waves) are the fastest earthquake waves, so they reach a seismograph first. They are longitudinal (compressional) waves, which travel through solids, liquids and gases.

 

• The order of arrival is P-waves, then S-waves (secondary waves), then surface waves (L-waves).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Secondary waves (S-waves) are transverse waves. They are slower than P-waves and travel only through solids. They cannot pass through the liquid outer core.

 

• Surface waves (Love waves and Rayleigh waves) are the slowest but cause the most damage on the Earth's surface.

 

• Shadow zone: P-waves are not recorded in the zone between about 105° and 145° from the epicentre. S-waves are not recorded beyond 105°.

 

• The point where an earthquake begins inside the Earth is the focus (hypocentre). The point on the surface directly above it is the epicentre. Earthquakes are measured with a seismograph (the Richter scale gives the magnitude and the Mercalli scale the intensity).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (Secondary waves moving through solids) is wrong: S-waves travel more slowly than P-waves.

 

• Option 3 (Surface waves causing severe destruction) is wrong: surface waves are the slowest, although they are the most destructive.

 

• Option 4 (Love waves disturbing ground horizontally) is wrong: Love waves are a type of surface wave and are slow.

 

• (Flagged: the wording "arriving first always" in Option 1 is loose, but P-waves are the fastest waves, so the PDF key is kept.)

question: The term "Bully" is a technical method used to restart play in which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Field Hockey.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The bully is a method of restarting play in field hockey. Two opposing players stand facing each other with the ball between them. They tap the ground and then each other's stick three times before they play the ball.

 

• In the modern rules of the game, the bully has been replaced by other restarts (a free hit or a pass-back), but it is still the term associated with field hockey.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Field hockey is played by two teams of 11 players each. India has won 8 Olympic gold medals in men's hockey. Major Dhyan Chand is known as the "Hockey Wizard", and his birthday, 29 August, is celebrated as National Sports Day.

 

• Hockey terms: penalty corner, short corner, striking circle (D), pass-back, push-in.

 

• The national game of India is often said to be hockey (it is not officially declared).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Basketball) is wrong: play in basketball restarts with a jump ball or a throw-in.

 

• Option 3 (Rugby) is wrong: rugby uses the scrum, the lineout and the ruck to restart play.

 

• Option 4 (Water Polo) is wrong: water polo uses a sprint (swim-off) to start each period.

 

• (Flagged: the "bully" has been replaced in the current hockey rules. The PDF key, Field Hockey, is kept.)

question: The term "Double Fault" is a common error resulting in the loss of a point in which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tennis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A double fault occurs in tennis when the server fails to make a legal serve twice in a row (two faults). The server then loses the point.

 

• A serve is a fault if the ball lands outside the correct service box, or if the server commits a foot fault.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The four Grand Slam tournaments are the Australian Open (hard court), the French Open (clay), Wimbledon (grass) and the US Open (hard court).

 

• Other tennis terms: ace (a serve that the receiver cannot touch), deuce (40–40), love (zero), let (a serve that touches the net and lands in the box, which is replayed).

 

• Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament (since 1877) and is played on grass courts.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Volleyball) is wrong: volleyball has the term "double contact" (a player hitting the ball twice in a row), not the double fault.

 

• Option 3 (Squash) is wrong: squash uses terms such as "let" and "stroke" and does not have a double fault.

 

• Option 4 (Billiards) is wrong: billiards is a cue sport in which players score by pocketing balls, so the term is not used there.

question: Who was the tribal revolutionary leader responsible for leading the Rampa Rebellion of 1922 against the British Forest Acts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alluri Sitarama Raju.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rampa Rebellion (1922–24) was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju in the Godavari agency area of present-day Andhra Pradesh. The tribals revolted against the Madras Forest Act, 1882, which restricted their right to move in forests and their traditional podu (shifting) cultivation.

 

• Alluri Sitarama Raju used guerrilla tactics and is known as "Manyam Veerudu" (Hero of the Jungle). He was captured and killed by the British in May 1924.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Madras Forest Act, 1882 and the Indian Forest Act, 1878 and 1927 limited the tribals' use of forests. The rebellion is also linked to the Non-Cooperation Movement period.

 

• Tribal revolts to remember: Santhal Hul (1855–56), Munda Ulgulan (1899–1900), Rampa Rebellion (1922), Gond uprising of Komaram Bheem (1940).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Birsa Munda) is wrong: he led the Munda Ulgulan (1899–1900) in the Chotanagpur region.

question: Who was the first Indian female athlete to win a gold medal at the Asian Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kamaljeet Sandhu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kamaljeet Sandhu was the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games gold medal. She won the 400 m race at the 1970 Asian Games in Bangkok.

 

• The Asian Games are held every four years under the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA). The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in 1951.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• M.D. Valsamma won the gold in the 400 m hurdles at the 1982 Asian Games in New Delhi.

 

• P.T. Usha (the "Payyoli Express") won four gold medals at the 1986 Asian Games in Seoul and narrowly missed an Olympic medal in the 400 m hurdles in 1984.

 

• Shiny Abraham (Wilson) became the first Indian woman to reach an Olympic semi-final in athletics (800 m, 1984 Los Angeles).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (P.T. Usha) is wrong: her first Asian Games gold medals came later, in 1986.

 

• Option 3 (Shiny Abraham) is wrong: she is known for reaching the Olympic semi-final in 1984, not as the first Asian Games gold medallist.

 

• Option 4 (M.D. Valsamma) is wrong: her Asian Games gold came in 1982, after Sandhu's gold in 1970.

question: Who became the Chairperson of the 8th Pay Commission in November 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Justice (Retd.) Ranjana Prakash Desai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Justice (Retd.) Ranjana Prakash Desai, a former judge of the Supreme Court, was appointed Chairperson of the 8th Central Pay Commission when its terms of reference were notified in November 2025.

 

• Prof. Pulak Ghosh (IIM Bangalore) is a part-time member and Pankaj Jain is the Member-Secretary. The Commission is to give its report within 18 months.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pay Commission reviews the pay, allowances and pensions of central government employees. The 7th Pay Commission (2014–16) was chaired by Justice A. K. Mathur and its recommendations took effect from 1 January 2016.

 

• The 7th Pay Commission's term was to end on 31 December 2025, so the 8th Pay Commission is meant to apply from 1 January 2026.

 

• The fitment factor is the multiplier used to convert the old basic pay into the new basic pay.

 

NOTE

question: Who was made the Director General (DG) of the Border Security Force (BSF) in January 2026?

• Praveen Kumar, an IPS officer, was appointed Director General of the Border Security Force (BSF) in January 2026.

 

• The BSF is a central armed police force under the Ministry of Home Affairs. It guards the India–Pakistan and India–Bangladesh borders. It was raised on 1 December 1965, and its first Director General was K. F. Rustamji.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

• BSF motto: "Jeevan Paryant Kartavya" (Duty unto Death). BSF Raising Day is 1 December. Its headquarters is in New Delhi.

 

• Other border-guarding forces: ITBP (India–China border, raised in 1962), SSB (India–Nepal and India–Bhutan borders), Assam Rifles (India–Myanmar border).

 

• Shatrujeet Singh Kapoor was appointed to head the ITBP in the same round of appointments.

question:
Fill in the blank:

The government identifies certain high-performing PSUs and grants them greater autonomy by giving them the status of 'Navratna' or '_'.
solution_text:

• The government grants greater autonomy to high-performing Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) by classifying them as Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna (Category I and Category II). The status that completes the blank here is Miniratna.

 

• The Navratna and Miniratna schemes were started in 1997. The Maharatna scheme was started in 2010.

 

• A PSU with a higher status can invest more in projects and joint ventures without prior government approval.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hierarchy (highest to lowest): Maharatna → Navratna → Miniratna Category I → Miniratna Category II.

 

• Maharatna companies can invest up to ₹5,000 crore (or 15% of their net worth) in a single project without government approval. Navratna companies can invest up to ₹1,000 crore.

 

• Examples: Maharatna – ONGC, NTPC, Coal India, SAIL. Navratna – HAL, BEL, NMDC. Miniratna – IRCTC, RailTel, MMTC.

• Option 4 (Heeraratna) is wrong: no such category exists for PSUs.
